## The trap

A preference stored **only in the desktop webview's `localStorage`** silently
fails to persist. The user changes it, it applies in-session, then on the next
reload/restart it's back to the default. Reported as *"the theme switch doesn't
persist"* (it was the active-theme selection; the same applies to any
localStorage-only pref).

It is **not** a bug in the read/write/apply code — that's usually correct. The
problem is that **localStorage in the Tauri/WebKitGTK webview is not a reliable
durable store on this app.** Three compounding reasons:

1. **Origin churn across launches (dominant).** The desktop binds a *random
   free* sidecar port each launch (`papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs`
   → `find_free_port()`), and the webview loads `http://localhost:<port>`.
   WebKitGTK partitions localStorage by **origin = scheme + host + port**, so
   **every launch on a new port = a brand-new, empty localStorage partition.**
   On a long-lived dev box you can see the history pile up:

   ```sh
   ls ~/.local/share/com.papercusp.desktop/localstorage/*.localstorage \
     | grep -oE 'localhost_[0-9]+' | sort -u | wc -l    # → dozens of ports
   ```

   (The `papercusp://localhost` custom protocol — default-on since 2026-06-01,
   `src-tauri/src/custom_protocol.rs` — gives the *packaged* app a **stable**
   origin while keeping the port dynamic. But the **dev shell loads the HTTP
   `devUrl` directly**, bypassing it, so dev still gets the unstable origin.)

2. **`localhost` vs `127.0.0.1` are different origins** → different partitions.
   `devUrl` (`http://localhost:3070`) and `frontendDist` (`http://127.0.0.1:3070`)
   do not share localStorage.

3. **In-session writes don't reliably flush across a reload.** Even on a fixed
   port, a `localStorage.setItem` followed (seconds later) by a real reload can
   come back empty — the on-disk SQLite stays un-checkpointed (observed a 34 MB
   abandoned `…localstorage-wal` whose main DB hadn't been written in a day),
   so the reload re-hydrates from a stale snapshot that lacks the write. Several
   `com.papercusp.desktop` instances sharing one WebKit data dir on a busy box
   makes this worse.

This is exactly why the storage policy says **per-user preferences belong in
Postgres, not localStorage** (see `/internal/docs/system/storage-policy`).

## The fix / the pattern

Make **Postgres the source of truth** and keep localStorage as a *non-authoritative
per-device cache* for instant first paint. The blessed in-repo pattern (already
used by `auto_accept` in `operator-shared-state.ts` and `toast_last_seen_ms` in
`NotificationCenter.tsx`, and generalized in `lib/profile-pref.ts`):

1. **First paint** — read the localStorage cache synchronously (instant).
2. **On mount** — `GET /api/profile`; if PG differs, adopt it (overwrite cache +
   apply + notify). `reconcileProfilePref()` does this, with a guard so a
   concurrent local edit isn't clobbered by a slow GET.
3. **On change** — write the cache + apply + notify, **and** `POST /api/profile`
   (fire-and-forget). PG is the durable copy.

For **pre-paint** prefs (theme, visual-effects — read before React mounts to
avoid a flash), the host **injects the PG value into `index.html`** alongside
`window.__PAPERCUSP_WS__` / `__PAPERCUSP_FLAGS__` (`apps/operator/bin/host-spa.ts`),
and the boot scripts read the injected value first, cache as fallback.

Adding a field is just a new key on the `operator_user_profile` JSONB (no SQL
migration) — extend the `Profile` type in `lib/session.ts` **and** the `ALLOWED`
allowlist in `endpoint-route/routes/misc/profile.ts` (the POST silently strips
keys not on the list).

## The React-snapshot gotcha (don't stop at host injection)

Host injection makes the **boot script** paint the right value — but React can
still reset it. `useSyncExternalStore`'s synchronous snapshot
(`readActiveTheme()` / `readVisualEffectsMode()`) reads the localStorage cache,
which is **cold right after a desktop reload**, so it falls back to the default
and overwrites the freshly-injected value on first render. data-theme flips
injected → default a beat after load.

Fix: the synchronous read must fall back **cache → injected
(`window.__PAPERCUSP_PREFS__`) → default**, so the snapshot agrees with what the
boot script painted. See `injectedPref()` in `lib/profile-pref.ts`.

## How to diagnose

- "Setting doesn't persist after reload" on the desktop → suspect localStorage,
  not your read/write logic. Confirm: drive the running webview's dev bridge
  (`tauri-agent-tools eval`), write the key, do a **genuine** reload
  (`window.__papercuspOriginalReload()` — `location.reload` is suppressed on the
  static host), then re-read. If a freshly-written key vanishes while *old* keys
  survive, it's the flush/origin problem, not your code.
- Inspect on disk: `~/.local/share/com.papercusp.desktop/localstorage/` — many
  `http_localhost_<port>.localstorage` files (one per past port) is the origin-churn
  smoking gun; a large, stale-mtime `…-wal` next to an old `.localstorage` is the
  unflushed-write smoking gun.

## Rule of thumb

If a value is a **per-user preference that should survive a reload/restart**, it
goes in **PG** (`operator_user_profile` via `/api/profile`), with localStorage
only as a pre-paint cache. localStorage-only is fine for **caches** (recomputable —
git logs, custom-theme CSS) and **ephemeral one-shot UI flags** (onboarding
"seen", hint dismissals), where losing it on a reset is harmless.

See `lib/profile-pref.ts`, `/internal/docs/system/storage-policy`, and the
related [headless-desktop-testing-needs-gl](/internal/docs/agent-insights/headless-desktop-testing-needs-gl)
insight for the desktop-webview context.
